data.name: Karawan
data.gender_notes: Karawan is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: A group of people or animals traveling together for protection, companionship, and survival. This name is derived from the Arabic root 'k-r-w' which means 'to travel' or 'to move'. It is a beautiful reminder of the journey of life and the importance of companionship and protection along the way. The name Karawan carries the meaning “Traveler's caravan” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Karawan usually hope their child will grow to embody traveler's caravan and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of the spiritual journey and companionship along the path.
data.etymology: Karawan belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Traveler's caravan.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Karawan total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

in_arabic.name: كاروان
in_arabic.long_meaning: كاروان هو اسم يطلق على جماعة من الناس يسافرون معاً، وغالباً ما يكونون على ظهر الجمال أو غيرها من الحيوانات، ويستخدم هذا الاسم في القرآن الكريم في سورة الفرقان الآية ٣٦، ويحمل هذا الاسم معاني التعاون والتضامن بين أفراد الجماعة، كما كان يطلق على القوافل التجارية في العصور القديمة.

in_urdu.name: کاروان
in_urdu.meaning: لوگوں کا ایک ساتھ سفر کرنے والا گروہ
in_urdu.long_meaning: کاروان کا مطلب ہے لوگوں کا ایک ساتھ سفر کرنے والا گروہ، خاص طور پر اونٹوں یا دیگر جانوروں پر سوار ہو کر سفر کرنے والے، یہ نام عربی جڑوں سے ماخوذ ہے اور اس کا تعلق قافلوں اور تجارتی سفر سے ہے، جنوبی ایشیاء میں مسلم روایت میں اس کا خاصا महत्व ہے.

in_hindi.name: कारवां
in_hindi.meaning: एक साथ यात्रा करने वाले लोगों का समूह
in_hindi.long_meaning: कारवां का अर्थ है एक साथ यात्रा करने वाले लोगों का समूह, विशेष रूप से ऊंटों या अन्य जानवरों पर सवार होकर यात्रा करने वाले, यह नाम अरबी मूल से लिया गया है और इसका संबंध काफिले और व्यापारिक यात्रा से है, भारतीय मुस्लिम समुदाय में इसका विशेष महत्व है.

in_pashto.name: کاروان
in_pashto.meaning: د خلکو يو ډله چې يو ځای ته سفر کوي
in_pashto.long_meaning: کاروان د خلکو یو ډله ده چې یو ځای ته سفر کوي، په ځانګړي ډول د اونټونو یا نورو حیواناتو پر سپریدو، دا نوم د عربي ريښو څخه اخیستل شوی دی او د قافلو او سوداګریزو سفرونو سره تړاو لري، د افغان او پښتون دودیزو ارزښتونو کې مهم ځای لري.

in_english.name: Karawan
in_english.meaning: a group of people traveling together
in_english.long_meaning: Karawan refers to a group of people traveling together, often on camels or other animals, the term originates from Arabic roots and is mentioned in the Quran, specifically in Surah Al-Furqan verse 36, it symbolizes cooperation and unity among travelers, historically used for trade caravans, and holds spiritual significance in Islamic tradition.

data.cultural_impact: The term "Karawan" holds a rich cultural significance, particularly in the Islamic tradition. It is an evocative reminder of the journeys undertaken by the early Muslims, known as the Muhajirun and Ansar, who traveled from their homes in Mecca to settle in Medina. These groups of people traveled in large caravans or "Karawan" for protection and companionship against the harsh desert landscape and the adversities that came with establishing a new community in a foreign land. The spirit of unity and mutual aid in the face of adversity is a powerful symbol of community and solidarity, which continues to resonate with Muslims today.
data.spiritual_significance: At a deeper spiritual level, the name "Karawan" can be seen as a metaphor for the journey of life itself. We are all travelers on a quest for knowledge, wisdom, and the divine presence. The name serves as a constant reminder to cherish the companionship and guidance of others, as we traverse the ups and downs of this earthly journey, knowing that like a "Karawan," our fate is intertwined with that of our brethren. May we be guided and protected by the Almighty on our journey, and may we offer the same to our fellow travelers.
